evidence.positive: Mayo SIU feed, case 900002 in mayo-mayo: sent an In Room SIU^S14 (OBX 'In Room' 20261110101318) via POST /api/admin/hl7-inbound-messages/send; the row was created with reportable_start_time 16:13:18Z. Set start_time to 16:13:18Z through PUT /api/admin/patients/99000002/operations/900002/dates to stand in for the case start In Room records (local case start fails on Epic FHIR). Sent Anes Start 20261110101300: row became start_time=2026-11-10 16:13:00+00, anesthesia_start_time=2026-11-10 16:13:00+00, log 'Case CaseId[value=900002] start time set to the anesthesia start at Tue Nov 10 16:13:00 UTC 2026'. Sent the Epic-style correction Anes Start 20261110101200: both columns moved to 16:12:00+00 with the matching log line. Earlier on case 900001 a later correction (10:01:30 after 09:59:00) also moved both columns to 16:01:30+00. MGB notification feed, demo tenant case 09234 (HOSPITAL=DEMO, ORL=09234): start_time pre-set to 15:00:28Z, then POST /api/integration/mgb/event with OR_EVENT_ID 70 Anesthesia Start OR_NEW_INSTANT 2026-11-10T15:00:00Z: row became start_time=15:00:00+00, anesthesia_start_time=15:00:00+00, log 'Case CaseId[value=09234] start time set to the anesthesia start at Tue Nov 10 15:00:00 UTC 2026'; correction to 14:59:00Z moved both columns again. Liquibase changesets 216-add-anesthesia-start-time-to-operations and 217-backfill-anesthesia-start-time show EXECUTED in databasechangelog for mayo-mayo, demo-demo and mgb-mgh, and the operations table has the anesthesia_start_time column.
evidence.negative: Non-anesthesia milestones leave the case start alone on both feeds. Mayo case 900002 after start_time=16:12:00: sent Proc Start 20261110102000 and an In Room resend 20261110102100; row stayed start_time=16:12:00+00, anesthesia_start_time=16:12:00+00, reportable_start_time=16:13:18+00 while procedure_start_time became 16:20:00+00, proving the messages were processed and only the anesthesia path writes the case start; the log shows 'Dispatched OR timing event' for both with no 'start time set to the anesthesia start' line. Demo/MGB case 09234 after start_time=14:59:00: sent OR_EVENT_ID 80 Procedure Start 15:05:00Z then OR_EVENT_ID 60 In Room 15:06:00Z; row stayed start_time=14:59:00+00, anesthesia_start_time=14:59:00+00 while procedure_start_time became 15:05:00+00 and reportable_start_time 15:06:00+00, no 'start time set' log line for either.
evidence.red_check: Ran the pre-fix code. Compiled the parent-commit (c0ff2e51d^1) MayoOperationEventService and MGHOperationEventService with Java 25 against the container's jars (MGH class with the unused @Slf4j removed), backed up the shipped MGHOperationEventService classes (md5 e8d6d920226ba89cce626b0593f1aeef), copied the pre-fix MGH classes over them in /app/classes and dropped the pre-fix Mayo classes into /app/classes/com/guided/orci/integration/mayo where they shadow the mayo-client-integration jar, then docker restart. Mayo case 900777: In Room 20261110103018, start_time set to 16:30:18Z, then Anes Start 20261110103000. Red: the dispatch logged 'Dispatched OR timing event Anes Start categories=[START_MONITORING]' and 'caseId=CaseId[value=900777], eventCategories=[START_MONITORING]', no 'start time set' line, row stayed start_time=16:30:18+00 with anesthesia_start_time NULL, which is exactly the ticket's bug. Demo/MGB case 09234: Anesthesia Start 14:50:00Z under the pre-fix classes logged 'caseId=CaseId[value=09234], eventCategories=[START_MONITORING]' and the row stayed at 14:59:00. Reverted: swap.sh restore copied the backups back, removed the shadow mayo directory, docker restart; md5 of the restored MGHOperationEventService.class is e8d6d920226ba89cce626b0593f1aeef (matches shipped) and the shadow directory is gone. Re-ran the positive after restore: Anes Start 10:30:00 on 900777 moved start_time and anesthesia_start_time to 16:30:00+00 with the 'start time set' log line, and MGB Anesthesia Start 14:50:00Z on 09234 moved both columns to 14:50:00+00.

caveats: The case start that In Room normally records could not come from the real startOperation path locally (Mayo case start needs Epic FHIR, MGB needs the SOAP surgical record); the pre-existing start_time was written through the admin operations/dates endpoint instead, so the overwrite was exercised against the real column and update statement but not the real first writer.
The MGB notification feed was exercised through the demo tenant (HOSPITAL=DEMO on /api/integration/mgb/event), not mgb-mgh; the handler and event map are the same for both.
Changeset 217 backfill ran against an empty database, so it is confirmed to execute in every tenant schema but not observed copying start_time into anesthesia_start_time for pre-existing rows.
The downstream effect on findOperationBasedOnStartTime (med admins in the gap attaching to the case) was not exercised.

The pre-fix MGHOperationEventService was compiled from the parent commit, which predates the later eventTypes attribution field, so eventTypes logged empty during the MGB red run; the event categories, which are the subject here, behaved as pre-fix.

automation.assessment: Unit coverage from the PR is solid: EventServiceTimingEventDispatchTest covers anesthesia start recording, In Room not touching it, and non-anesthesia milestones never recording it; MGHOperationEventServiceTest covers the MGB map; OperationRepositoryTest covers the update writing both columns, replacing a case start from another milestone, later corrections, and lastModifiedDate. What is not locked in is the Mayo SIU processor end to end (MayoHL7SiuCaseSchedulingProcessorTest asserts attribution for Anes Start but not that ANESTHESIA_START_TIME is dispatched) and the earlier-correction direction at the repository level.
proposed_tests: MayoHL7SiuCaseSchedulingProcessorTest: an Anes Start SIU dispatches handleTimingEvent with both START_MONITORING and ANESTHESIA_START_TIME, and an In Room SIU dispatches without ANESTHESIA_START_TIME.
OperationRepositoryTest: updateAnesthesiaStartTime accepts a correction that moves the time earlier (the ticket's 13:13:00 to 13:12:00 example), mirroring the existing later-correction test.

qa-suite supplemental (Mayo tenant on an environment where it is enabled): inject In Room then Anes Start then a corrected Anes Start through the admin HL7 send endpoint and assert the operation's startTime via the admin operations API equals the final anesthesia time.

jira_comment:
Verdict: deploy-ready.

Positive: An Anes Start SIU on a Mayo case and an Anesthesia Start notification on an MGB-feed case each set the case start and anesthesia_start_time to the anesthesia time, and a corrected Anes Start moved both columns again in either direction.
Negative: Proc Start and a resent In Room on the same cases wrote their own columns but left the case start and anesthesia_start_time untouched.
Red check: With the pre-fix event-map classes swapped into the container, the same Anes Start dispatched only the monitoring category and the case start stayed at the In Room time; the shipped classes were restored by checksum and the positive re-ran green.

Automation: Unit coverage from the PR is solid; a processor-level Mayo SIU dispatch test and an earlier-correction repository test are proposed.
